title: Certifying strategyproof auction networks

title: In congestion games, taxes achieve optimal approximation

title: Counterspeculation, auctions, and competitive sealed tenders

title: Automated Design of Affine Maximizer Mechanisms in Dynamic Settings

title: Improved metric distortion via threshold approvals

title: Multitask Peer Prediction With Task-dependent Strategies

title: Eliciting Informative Text Evaluations with Large Language Models
code_note: Informativeness of textual reports, not explanation generation. Do not claim dominant truthfulness, arbitrary LLM accuracy, or that natural language itself ensures explanation fidelity.

title: A Bayesian Truth Serum for Subjective Data

title: Eliciting Informative Feedback: The Peer-Prediction Method

title: The Dynamic Pivot Mechanism

title: An Efficient Dynamic Mechanism
code_note: Dynamic allocation/payment and participation rules. Do not conflate ex-post IC of the unbalanced construction with all guarantees of the balanced mechanism.

title: Regret minimization in online Bayesian persuasion: Handling adversarial receiver's types under full and partial feedback models
code_note: Signaling policy and persuasiveness constraints. Learning regret is not auction unilateral-deviation regret; not a repeated-user explanation-comprehension experiment.

title: Encoding Human Behavior in Information Design through Deep Learning
code_note: Behavior-sensitive signaling policy. Human-subject policy performance is not by itself proof of explanation fidelity or reduced cognitive burden.

title: Information Design in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Markov signaling policy. Agent compliance is not human comprehensibility; learned signaling is not intrinsically benign or transparent.

title: Algorithmic Information Design in Multi-Player Games: Possibilities and Limits in Singleton Congestion

title: Information Design for Congestion Games with Unknown Demand

title: Catastrophe by Design in Population Games: A Mechanism to Destabilize Inefficient Locked-in Technologies

title: FACT or Fiction: Can Truthful Mechanisms Eliminate Federated Free Riding?
